This duality allows for reduction of high-dimensional measure-theoretic problems into lower-dimensional ones. For a non-negative measurable function h on X × Y, Fubini's theorem enables expressing the integral as an iterated integral, which is foundational for probabilistic and statistical modeling in multi-dimensional domains. The failure mode arises when the function lacks measurability or when the underlying spaces are not σ-finite, breaking the applicability of these characterizations.
